paper.title: Agent Workflow Memory
paper.central_claim: Inducing reusable subtask workflows from trajectories and retaining them in agent memory improves long-horizon web navigation, in offline and supervision-free online settings, and generalizes across tasks, websites and domains.

provenance.notes: Assigned model type sonnet maps to gpt-6.1-sol; environment identifies gpt-6.1-sol. No independent runtime receipt or session identifier exposed; actual_model left null per worker template. No model probing.

sections_read: Full fixed HTML text lines 1–2866: abstract, §§1–7, all tables 1–11, Appendix A prompts/examples/quality, B rule induction, C mixed offline/online

evidence.quote: Moreover, as agents solve each task separately, they do not learn from past successes and failures, and are therefore unable to adapt over time
evidence.support_explanation: Author states fixed per-task examples and absent cross-task experience as the gap.

evidence.quote: These workflows are segmented (based on double-line breaks in the model output) and stored separately in the workflow memory.
evidence.support_explanation: Parameterized subroutines become explicit persistent text entries.

evidence.quote: Since the workflows are fully induced before test-time inference, the agent uses the same workflow memory
evidence.support_explanation: Offline variant freezes the training-induced store before test tasks.

evidence.quote: We evaluate the success rate of the predicted action trajectories
evidence.support_explanation: Online gains aggregate the same stream used for updating the store; do not treat that stream as independent heldout certification.

evidence.quote: Most importantly, WebArena supports rigorous evaluation on the functional correctness of agent trajectories.
evidence.support_explanation: Task outcome metric has an execution-based benchmark anchor, unlike the online write gate which uses a neural success classifier.
Author-reported WebArena task SR 35.5%, versus BrowserGym 23.5% or matched-observation ax-tree 15.0%; not our reproduction.

evidence.quote: by grouping examples by their templates and randomly choosing one example from each template group.
evidence.support_explanation: Cross-template subset removes same-template repetition; Table 2 reports 33.2 vs 20.5 ax-tree on 197 tasks, but updates continue within that subset.

evidence.quote: using rule- and LM-based workflow induction performs comparably
evidence.support_explanation: 35.6 rule vs 35.5 LM means abstraction-specific advantage is not established for WebArena; Mind2Web Table 6 favors LM.

evidence.quote: induces workflows from model-predicted trajectories that are not always correct, thus can lead to incorrect workflows that degrade model performance.
evidence.support_explanation: Self-judge gate can admit bad workflows; no measured marginal admission/retirement test is specified.

evidence.quote: Interestingly, using both NL and filtered HTML leads to worse results.
evidence.support_explanation: Reports representation failure and context-noise boundary, not uniformly positive outcomes.

evidence.quote: the action to choose pop-up airports is executed without seeing the intermediate states with available pop-up options, and is not flexible enough to do so.
evidence.support_explanation: Executable macro variant lacks intermediate observation; main contribution remains contextual workflows, not verified general callable skills.

evidence.quote: workflows induced offline and online are not fully compatible with each other
evidence.support_explanation: Mixing stores can impair utility; Appendix C supplies negative evidence against monotonic accumulation.

signatures.object: Textual workflow memory appended to system/auxiliary prompt
signatures.information: Task instruction, webpage observations, trajectory and LM binary success judgment; offline variant additionally sees canonical training trajectories. No benchmark ground-truth evaluator is stated as the online write gate.
signatures.operation: Extract frequently recurring subtasks, replace instance values with slots, segment workflows, append to site-specific memory; inject in future action generation.
signatures.output: Goal description plus state/thought/action workflow text
signatures.conditions: Repeated reusable subroutines and sufficiently reliable success judgment; per-website grouping limits memory relevance.
signatures.feedback: LM success classifier for online trajectories; supplied canonical examples offline
signatures.selection_rule: Only predicted-success trajectories are induced; prompt asks for non-overlapping workflows of at least two steps. No per-entry marginal utility gate or rollback.
signatures.selection_data: Completed earlier tasks in the test stream (online) or training examples (offline)
signatures.persistence: Workflow memory M^t→M^(t+1); fixed offline memory, append online
signatures.later_use: Next streamed instruction receives accumulated workflows in its context
signatures.claimed_effect: WebArena 35.5% SR, Mind2Web offline GPT-4 step SR 45.1%; cross-template/cross-domain results
signatures.failure_boundary: Wrong self-judged successes poison workflows; actions can over-follow irrelevant routines; mixed stores interfere.

gap.author_gap: Fixed demonstrations do not abstract reusable subroutines or adapt between tasks.
gap.checked_gap: Specific contrast to full concrete Synapse trajectories and hand-authored SteP workflows is meaningful; replacing instance values and inducing subtasks directly addresses reuse rather than merely claiming frozen-weight learning.

lineage.source_version: cited within fixed 2409.07429v1 §§3.2/6; primary neighbor not supplied
as discussed in §6; no independent primary text fixed

gap.closest_adjacent: Synapse precedent retrieval; SteP authored routines; BrowserGym fixed agent scaffold.
gap.residue: Need automatic reusable, parameterized subtasks without canonical aligned examples.
gap.stakes: Long action sequences, brittle element/action transfer and cost.
gap.method_response: Slot abstraction plus success-filtered online induction changes what memory contains and when it is written.
gap.remaining_gap: No durable maintenance/retirement; independent online certification and full budget controls remain weak.
unresolved: Request primary fixed Synapse, SteP and Voyager sources for independent closest-neighbor novelty/lineage verification; only this paper’s descriptions available.

tactic_steps_checked: Canonical parameterized workflow schema and accumulated reference substrate explicitly used at inference; no upstream format training required by the parent.
C03 structural category-holdout ideal only partly met: offline tasks separate; online evaluation adapts within target streams.
Rule-induced workflows and Synapse are simpler-conditioning controls.
success/failure_checks: Offline heldout and cross-template tests help, but online cross-domain is not a frozen unseen-domain transfer test.
A trained first-class conditioning channel is not claimed and is not imposed as an inapplicable requirement.
matches.reason: Memory is the inference conditioning substrate; C03 fits reference-substrate branch but online leakage and missing matched budget bound execution quality.

rs_pattern.reason: Actual operation is parameter-free adaptation by workflow conditioning.

condition_checks.reason: Fixed full-example memory becomes induced parameterized routines.
Self-judged gate is explicit and its errors acknowledged.
Append-only workflow memory; no explicit forgetting/rollback described.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Trajectory-derived parameterized routines become the reference context for later tasks.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: H00 abstractions fit better than raw H03 precedent indexing; main method does not certify executable macro generality, so H06 not assigned.

expectations.reason: Gate exists, but admits incorrect traces and is not externally calibrated here.
No explicit consolidation, retirement or rollback policy; incompatibility is observed.
Cross-template test and offline training/test split help; online target stream still constructs and evaluates memory.
Rule and LM match WebArena; Mind2Web supports scoped abstraction benefit.

expectations.applies_when: Efficiency claim includes induction and retention work.
expectations.reason: Execution steps reported but not full induction dollar/token/call cost.

claims.baseline/control: BrowserGym ax-tree and full BrowserGym; MindAct, Synapse, rule induction.
claims.selection_vs_test: Offline frozen training-induced memory is tested on separate tasks; online evaluates and updates within test streams.
claims.result/denominator: Table 1 35.5 vs 15.0 ax-tree / 23.5 BrowserGym; Table 2 cross-template 33.2 vs 20.5 on 197 tasks; Table 3 GPT-4 step 45.1 vs 36.2 but task 4.8 vs 2.0.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported workflow conditioning improves these benchmark protocols; not a blanket unbiased continual-learning estimate.

claims.text: Abstract induction is the key reusable mechanism.
claims.result/denominator: WebArena 35.6 rule vs 35.5 LM, Mind2Web 43.4 vs 45.1 step SR; hybrid representation and mixed memories can hurt.
counterevidence: WebArena not better for LM abstraction
claims.allowed_conclusion: Abstraction advantage is task-dependent; not universally superior to cheaper induction.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported frozen offline workflow memory improves later heldout Mind2Web tasks; online retained workflows improve aggregate navigation under a self-judged streaming protocol, with cross-template checks but no independent frozen online test. No improver-level claim supported.
unresolved: No full matched-cost or repeated stream-order uncertainty.

G.reason: Concrete reusable-subroutine gap and named neighbors; independent neighbor primary-source verification absent.

M.reason: Parameterized workflow induction and next-task conditioning target the stated transfer bottleneck, with alternative formats/inducers tested.

X.reason: Online write/read chain reconstructible; noisy judge, no retirement/rollback, and mixed-store interference leave growth conditions incomplete.

E.measurement.reason: Functional WebArena evaluation and defined Mind2Web step/task metrics; broad denominators. Metrics are meaningful but HTML text/§5 prose has an internal result inconsistency and self-judge write gate is not a gold metric.

E.causality.reason: Same-model baseline and rule/text/HTML ablations are informative; no fully budget-matched store-off loop, rule matches LM on WebArena.

E.holdout.reason: Offline frozen memory and cross-template subset support some retention; online updates on evaluation stream cannot certify clean domain transfer.

E.statistics.reason: Large task counts and negative outcomes, but no repeated stream-order variance or main-result confidence intervals (A2).
search_scope: Entire §§3–5 and Appendices A–C; uncertainty/seed/order/repeated-run reporting

E.cost.reason: Successful-task action counts reported; no complete induction/evaluation/token expenditure including failed tasks and gate costs.
search_scope: §3.1.1 steps, Appendix A workflow size/utility, §§4–5 and Appendices A–C cost reporting

reason: Complete fixed text read; retained offline benefit supported with scoped online claims. Missing neighbor primary texts recorded, not hidden or replaced by external searches.
